correctness.rationale: Fan--Li's Proposition 3.6 gives W->H as a Zariski-locally-trivial affine-line torsor and H=Tot_P(L⊕Q); homotopy invariance gives CH^*(W)=CH^*(P). The scheme-theoretic identity F=W×_H H_0 with H_0=Tot_P(Q) gives the same for F. Since H_0 is the zero divisor of the tautological section of L=O_P(-1), flat pullback gives O_W(F)=rho^*L, hence [F]=-h and N_{F/W}=rho_F^*O(-1). Smoothness then identifies Pic(W) with CH^1(W). No finite experiment is used.

value.rationale: The exceptional divisor is the geometric carrier of the unique birational modification. Identifying its integral class and normal bundle determines the entire exceptional intersection algebra and Picard generator, which is strictly finer than the paper's Euler/Grothendieck-class data and is a natural invariant for subsequent birational and intersection-theoretic work. The claim is uniform in n and is not a parameter spot-check or a recomputation of a known table.
